name: CALVIN
summary: CALVIN evaluates chains of up to five language-specified subtasks executed consecutively from unstructured play data, across four environments with a held-out split testing transfer to an environment never seen in training. Its long-horizon structure and the notorious difficulty of that zero-shot split made it the benchmark of choice for video-pretrained policies such as GR-1.
innovation: Sequential multi-subtask evaluation, which exposes the error compounding that single-task metrics hide.
An explicit unseen-environment split that forces generalization claims to be earned.
matters: One of the few benchmarks measuring long-horizon language grounding rather than isolated skills.
limits: Simulation only, with a single fixed arm and a small object set.
lineage: The language-conditioned long-horizon branch of manipulation benchmarking.
